PullRequest.Title: Align comment author and timestamp labels
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #143805 The Comments tree rendered the author at the body text size while the relative timestamp used fractional `0.9em` sizing. Browser rounding made their baselines drift at different zoom levels. This assigns both metadata fields the shared `body1` type role and adds a real `CommentNodeRenderer` fixture at 100% and 125% zoom across light, dark, and high-contrast themes. ## Before / After
BeforeAfter (125% zoom)
## Validation - `npm run eslint -- src/vs/workbench/test/browser/componentFixtures/comments/commentTree.fixture.ts` - `npm run stylelint -- src/vs/workbench/contrib/comments/browser/media/panel.css` - `npm run transpile-client` - Verified matching metadata baselines at 100% and 125% zoom

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening, scrolling, or repainting the Comments panel with rendered comment rows
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The virtualized comments tree creates/reuses visible row DOM, writes metadata text, and the browser resolves the added font-size declarations before layout and paint. The diff adds no JavaScript, geometry reads, timers, or extra layout pass; only the computed font-size value changes.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective cardinality is the number of currently rendered virtualized comment rows, not the total comment count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single browser UI thread; tree virtualization limits DOM/style work to rendered rows rather than all comments.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No application cache is added or bypassed. Normal browser selector/style caching applies; the rules are static and reused across rows.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the rule participates in style resolution on each visible comment row; high confidence that it does not introduce synchronous layout reads, repeated reconstruction, retained state, or an external boundary.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact number of visible rows and browser style-resolution duration varies, but the added two static selectors do not establish a measurable scaling regression beyond ordinary per-visible-row style matching.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The production change changes computed typography on existing nodes without increasing render frequency, DOM cardinality, layout passes, or boundary calls.

Scenarios.Scenario: Rendering the new comment metadata component fixtures at 100% and 125% zoom across dark, light, and high-contrast themes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: For each selected fixture variant, the fixture adapter installs themes and deterministic time, creates test services, renders one CommentNodeRenderer row, and disposes the renderer/services after capture. Theme setup must complete before fixture rendering; screenshot capture is downstream.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch the bundled default file-icon theme resource when the component-fixture process has a cold file-icon-theme cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one cold fetch for the shared default file-icon theme across all new variants because ensureFileIconThemeLoaded uses a module-level WeakMap; zero on warm cache. Color-theme JSON is bundled in memory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Before the diff these comment fixtures did not exist, so they did not invoke fixture setup; however the same globally cached setup is already used by every existing component fixture and the added variants do not fan it out per theme.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The single cold fetch can delay the first fixture render; subsequent variants reuse the resolved promise.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed eight registered theme variants total; only the zoomed fixture's four variants carry blocks-ci. Each variant renders one comment with no replies.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Fixture variants may be scheduled by the component-fixture host, while each variant performs one row render. There is no per-comment concurrency or unbounded task creation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Color-theme loads are cached per ColorThemeData and use bundled JSON. The default file-icon theme load is cached globally per FileIconThemeData, coalescing concurrent/cold variants onto one promise; warm variants perform no fetch.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the bounded fixture multiplicity, shared theme caches, one-row renderer path, and disposal ownership from the fixture adapter and explicit renderer cleanup.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: CI scheduling and whether another fixture warms the shared theme cache first vary, but total new fixture work is fixed to two fixture definitions with four theme variants each and one rendered row per variant.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added work is test-only, fixed-cardinality, uses coalesced theme loading, and explicitly disposes renderer templates and test services; it does not affect product startup or runtime.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the complete two-file diff. Checked production style/layout behavior, virtualized-row scaling, fixture variant multiplicity, theme-loading boundaries and caches, concurrency, and disposal lifecycle. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression was found.
